warli.name: Warli Art
warli.intro: Warli Art is a distinctive folk painting tradition associated with the Warli community of Maharashtra. It uses simple geometric forms to represent people, nature, celebrations and everyday community life.
warli.history: Warli painting developed as part of the visual traditions of communities living in parts of Maharashtra. Traditionally, paintings were created on walls during important social and ceremonial occasions. Over time, Warli art moved beyond traditional walls and became recognised through exhibitions, textiles, illustrations and contemporary artworks.

symbols.title: Circle
symbols.text: Often associated with natural and cyclical elements such as the sun and moon.

symbols.title: Triangle
symbols.text: Commonly used to construct human figures, trees and other forms.

symbols.title: Human Figures
symbols.text: Represent dancing, farming, celebrations and community activities.

symbols.title: Nature
symbols.text: Trees, animals and landscapes reflect the relationship between community and environment.

timeline.text: Warli paintings were closely connected with community life, rituals and ceremonial spaces.
The art form became increasingly recognised outside its traditional setting.
Warli motifs appear in paintings, textiles, illustrations, décor and contemporary creative work.

warli.today: Today, Warli Art continues to evolve while retaining its recognizable geometric visual language. Artists use the tradition in paintings, textiles, home décor, illustrations and other contemporary formats.
warli.preservation: Learning about the cultural context of Warli Art and supporting artists who continue the tradition can help preserve this important cultural practice.

paithani.name: Paithani
paithani.intro: Paithani is a celebrated handwoven textile tradition of Maharashtra, particularly associated with the town of Paithan. It is known for detailed weaving, rich colours and distinctive decorative motifs.
paithani.history: Paithani developed as an important textile tradition in Maharashtra and became associated with skilled handweaving and elaborate designs. The tradition has been passed through generations of weavers and continues to be valued for its craftsmanship.

symbols.title: Peacock
symbols.text: A popular decorative motif found in Paithani designs.

symbols.title: Muniya
symbols.text: A traditional parrot-inspired motif used in Paithani weaving.

symbols.title: Floral Motifs
symbols.text: Flowers and plant-inspired patterns contribute to the decorative vocabulary.

symbols.title: Pallu
symbols.text: The richly designed end section is one of the most recognizable parts of a Paithani saree.

timeline.text: Paithani developed as a significant textile tradition in Maharashtra.
Weaving knowledge and design practices continued through artisan families and communities.
Paithani remains an important traditional textile while contemporary designs have expanded its use.

paithani.today: Paithani continues to be valued as a traditional textile and is worn during weddings, festivals and cultural occasions. Contemporary variations also adapt traditional motifs and colour combinations.
paithani.preservation: Supporting genuine handwoven Paithani and learning about the work of traditional weavers helps sustain the craft and the communities connected to it.

chitrakathi.name: Chitrakathi
chitrakathi.intro: Chitrakathi is a traditional narrative art associated with Maharashtra in which painted images are used to visually communicate stories and episodes from cultural and religious traditions.
chitrakathi.history: Chitrakathi developed as part of a storytelling tradition in which visual images helped communicate stories to audiences. The practice is associated with communities of traditional storytellers and has been preserved through generations.
chitrakathi.surface: Hand-painted paper and other traditional surfaces

symbols.title: Characters
symbols.text: Figures help communicate important parts of a story.

symbols.title: Scenes
symbols.text: Different visual scenes can be arranged to communicate narrative events.

symbols.title: Expressions
symbols.text: Stylized gestures and expressions help viewers understand the story.

symbols.title: Symbols
symbols.text: Objects and visual elements can carry cultural or narrative meaning.

significance: Connects visual art with cultural stories

timeline.text: Painted images were connected with storytelling and cultural performances.
Traditional artists and communities continued passing the visual language across generations.
Chitrakathi is increasingly explored as an important part of Maharashtra's folk-art heritage.

chitrakathi.today: Today, Chitrakathi is valued as a cultural art tradition and is studied, exhibited and preserved through cultural initiatives and artisan communities.
chitrakathi.preservation: Documenting traditional practices and supporting artists and storytellers can help keep Chitrakathi alive for future generations.

sawantwadi.name: Sawantwadi Craft
sawantwadi.intro: Sawantwadi is known for traditional decorative crafts, particularly handcrafted wooden objects and painted products featuring detailed motifs and colourful designs.
sawantwadi.history: Traditional craft practices developed in the Sawantwadi region through skilled artisan communities. Craft objects have been used for decoration and cultural expression, with techniques being passed from one generation to another.

symbols.title: Floral Motifs
symbols.text: Flowers and plant-inspired patterns are commonly used for decoration.

symbols.title: Birds
symbols.text: Bird forms are used as decorative elements in traditional craft designs.

symbols.title: Nature
symbols.text: Natural forms influence many decorative patterns.

symbols.title: Traditional Patterns
symbols.text: Repeated decorative elements create visual identity.

timeline.text: Craft knowledge developed within artisan communities of the Sawantwadi region.
Techniques and decorative knowledge were passed between generations.
Traditional craft products continue to be made while adapting to contemporary markets.

sawantwadi.today: Sawantwadi craft continues through artisan workshops and cultural initiatives. Traditional techniques are also used to create decorative objects suited to contemporary homes and collectors.
sawantwadi.preservation: Buying authentic handmade products and supporting local artisans can contribute to the continuation of traditional craft skills.

kolhapuri.name: Kolhapuri Craft
kolhapuri.intro: Kolhapuri craft is strongly associated with the traditional handmade leather footwear and craft practices of Maharashtra, particularly the Kolhapur region.
kolhapuri.history: Traditional leather craftsmanship developed through skilled artisan communities in and around Kolhapur. Handmade footwear became particularly associated with the region and developed a distinctive identity through traditional construction and decorative details.

symbols.title: Traditional Form
symbols.text: The recognizable footwear form represents the craft's regional identity.

symbols.title: Hand Stitching
symbols.text: Traditional construction techniques reflect artisan skill.

symbols.title: Leather Texture
symbols.text: The natural character of leather contributes to the appearance of handmade products.

symbols.title: Regional Identity
symbols.text: The craft is closely associated with Kolhapur and Maharashtra.

significance: Connects everyday products with cultural identity

timeline.text: Leather-working skills developed within artisan communities of the Kolhapur region.
Handmade footwear became strongly associated with Kolhapur.
Kolhapuri-style footwear is recognised widely while artisans continue traditional handmade practices.

kolhapuri.today: Kolhapuri craft continues to combine traditional handmade methods with contemporary styles and markets. The craft remains an important part of Maharashtra's artisan heritage.
kolhapuri.preservation: Supporting genuine handmade products and responsible artisan businesses can help preserve traditional craftsmanship and provide sustainable opportunities for craft communities.

rajasthani-miniature.name: Rajasthani Miniature Painting
rajasthani-miniature.intro: Rajasthani Miniature Painting is a richly detailed painting tradition known for vibrant colours, decorative patterns, expressive figures and stories inspired by royal life, mythology, nature and poetry.
rajasthani-miniature.history: Rajasthani miniature painting developed through several regional schools and received strong support from Rajput courts. Artists created detailed paintings depicting royal portraits, court scenes, battles, festivals, religious stories and everyday life.

symbols.title: Peacock
symbols.text: Often represents beauty, nature and grace.

symbols.title: Lotus
symbols.text: Associated with purity, beauty and spiritual traditions.

symbols.title: Royal Figures
symbols.text: Represent the courtly culture and historical life of Rajasthan.

symbols.title: Nature
symbols.text: Trees, gardens, animals and landscapes create rich visual settings.

significance: Connects art with literature and mythology

timeline.text: Miniature traditions developed under regional kingdoms and artistic communities.
Rajput courts supported artists and encouraged detailed paintings of royal life, mythology and literature.
Different regional schools became recognized for their distinctive styles and subjects.
Artists continue the tradition through handmade paintings, exhibitions and contemporary interpretations.

rajasthani-miniature.today: Today, Rajasthani miniature painting continues to be practiced by traditional and contemporary artists. The style is also used in modern artworks, exhibitions, cultural education and heritage preservation.
rajasthani-miniature.preservation: Preservation efforts include supporting traditional artists, teaching miniature techniques to younger generations, documenting regional schools and encouraging exhibitions and cultural programs.

phad.name: Phad Painting
phad.intro: Phad Painting is a traditional Rajasthani scroll painting style that combines visual storytelling with folk traditions. Large painted scrolls narrate stories of local heroes, deities and legendary figures.
phad.history: Phad painting has been traditionally associated with storytelling communities of Rajasthan. Painted scrolls were used as visual narratives during performances in which storytellers presented stories of heroic and religious figures.

symbols.title: Heroic Figures
symbols.text: Represent legendary heroes and important cultural stories.

symbols.title: Horses
symbols.text: Often associated with journeys, battles and heroic narratives.

symbols.title: Temples
symbols.text: Represent sacred spaces and religious traditions.

symbols.title: Community Scenes
symbols.text: Show social life and collective cultural traditions.

timeline.text: Phad scrolls were created as visual storytelling tools for traditional performers.
Artists and storytellers passed the techniques and narratives through generations.
Artists and cultural institutions helped introduce Phad painting to wider audiences.
Phad artists create traditional scrolls as well as smaller artworks for exhibitions and collectors.

phad.today: Phad painting continues as both a traditional storytelling form and a contemporary art practice. Artists now create scrolls, paintings and educational works that introduce the tradition to new audiences.
phad.preservation: Supporting traditional Phad artists, documenting stories, conducting workshops and encouraging younger artists to learn the technique can help preserve this heritage.

mandana.name: Mandana Art
mandana.intro: Mandana is a traditional decorative art practiced in parts of Rajasthan and nearby regions. Geometric and symbolic designs are created on floors and walls during festivals, ceremonies and special occasions.
mandana.history: Mandana developed as a community-based decorative tradition connected with domestic spaces, festivals and rituals. Designs were traditionally created by women using locally available materials.

symbols.title: Lotus
symbols.text: Often associated with beauty, purity and auspicious occasions.

symbols.title: Peacock
symbols.text: Represents beauty, nature and celebration.

symbols.title: Geometric Forms
symbols.text: Create balance, rhythm and symmetry within the composition.

symbols.title: Floral Motifs
symbols.text: Connect decorative designs with nature and seasonal traditions.

timeline.text: Mandana designs were created in homes and community spaces during important occasions.
Knowledge of patterns and techniques was passed from one generation to another.
Mandana gained wider attention through folk-art documentation and cultural programs.
Artists reinterpret Mandana patterns on paper, fabric, walls and other surfaces.

mandana.today: Mandana continues to be practiced during festivals and ceremonies while contemporary artists adapt its geometric vocabulary to modern surfaces and designs.
mandana.preservation: Teaching Mandana in cultural workshops, documenting traditional motifs and supporting folk artists can help maintain this community-based art tradition.

blue-pottery.name: Blue Pottery
blue-pottery.intro: Rajasthan's Blue Pottery is a distinctive decorative craft known for its blue and turquoise designs, floral patterns and smooth glazed surfaces. Jaipur became especially associated with this craft.
blue-pottery.history: Blue pottery developed in Jaipur through influences from Central Asian, Persian and other artistic traditions. Local craftsmen adapted the technique and developed a recognizable regional style.

symbols.title: Floral Motifs
symbols.text: Flowers and vines create decorative compositions inspired by nature.

symbols.title: Birds
symbols.text: Bird motifs add movement and natural imagery to decorative surfaces.

symbols.title: Geometric Patterns
symbols.text: Repeated forms provide balance and structure.

symbols.title: Blue Tones
symbols.text: Blue and turquoise shades are strongly associated with the identity of Jaipur Blue Pottery.

timeline.text: The craft developed through artistic influences arriving from regions outside Rajasthan.
Local craftsmen adapted the technique and established a distinctive Jaipur style.
Blue pottery became increasingly recognized as an important Jaipur handicraft.
Artisans produce traditional and contemporary decorative objects for local and global audiences.

blue-pottery.today: Blue pottery is practiced by artisan families and craft workshops in Rajasthan. Along with traditional vessels, contemporary decorative products are also created.
blue-pottery.preservation: Supporting artisan workshops, providing craft education and encouraging responsible purchasing of handmade products can help sustain Blue Pottery traditions.

thewa.name: Thewa Art
thewa.intro: Thewa is a traditional Rajasthani craft that combines intricately worked gold with coloured glass. The technique is especially associated with Pratapgarh and is known for delicate decorative scenes and patterns.
thewa.history: Thewa developed as a specialized craft tradition in Rajasthan and became associated with skilled artisan families. The technique involves creating fine gold designs and fusing them with specially prepared coloured glass.

symbols.title: Floral Designs
symbols.text: Flowers and vines create elegant decorative compositions.

symbols.title: Royal Scenes
symbols.text: Historical and courtly scenes reflect Rajasthan's cultural heritage.

symbols.title: Birds & Animals
symbols.text: Natural motifs are frequently incorporated into decorative designs.

symbols.title: Traditional Patterns
symbols.text: Detailed motifs represent the skill and identity of Thewa craftsmanship.

timeline.text: Thewa developed as a specialized craft practiced by skilled artisan families.
The intricate craft gained recognition through traditional jewellery and decorative objects.
Thewa became increasingly recognized as a distinctive heritage craft of Rajasthan.
Artisans continue producing jewellery and decorative pieces while maintaining traditional techniques.

thewa.today: Thewa remains a specialized craft practiced by skilled artisans. Contemporary jewellery and decorative pieces continue to use traditional gold-and-glass techniques.
thewa.preservation: Preserving Thewa requires supporting skilled artisans, documenting traditional techniques, training new craftspeople and creating sustainable markets for authentic handmade work.
